extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office primary and assistant patent examiners (allowance/issue processing)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on preparing allowed patent applications for issue, including labeling, selecting claims/figures for printing, listing references, statements of reasons for allowance, Notices of Allowance, and post-allowance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class and subclass notation on file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid the Publishing Division and the printers, examiners should write the class and subclass on the outside of the file wrapper (for non-IFW applications) as carefully and legibly as possible. Each numeral should be distinct and any decimal point should be shown clearly and in its proper position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class and subclass written in pencil on any paper file wrapper should correspond to the class and subclass in which the patent will issue; the examiner's name written should correspond to the name of the examiner preparing the application for issue. See MPEP § 202.02 and § 202.03 for related notations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and update prior-application bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review the data regarding prior U.S. applications, parent applications, and prior provisional and foreign applications to make sure the information is correct when preparing the application for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claim to domestic priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) is added, deleted, or modified during prosecution and approved, update the file wrapper label or PALM bib-data sheet and the PALM database. If PALM has not been updated, forward the application (A) to the Office of Initial Patent Examination Customer Corrections with a completed Application Branch Data Base Routing Slip if application has a file jacket label and is 08/ or earlier series, or (B) to the Technology Center Legal Instrument Examiner with explanation (e.g., marked-up bib-data sheet) if IFW or 09/ or later; add a copy of the corrected bib-data sheet to the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record claim(s) selected for printing — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners preparing a non-IFW application for issue are to record the number of the claim selected for printing in the Official Gazette in the box labeled 'PRINT CLAIM' on the face of the file wrapper, or if IFW application, on the Issue Classification sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recording, write the claim number clearly in black ink; if multiple claims are selected, separate numbers with commas; refer to the renumbered patent claim number rather than the original application claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rules for claim(s) to print
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims should be selected in accordance with these instructions: (A) The broadest claim should be selected. (B) Examiners should ordinarily designate but one claim on each invention, although when a plurality of inventions are claimed in an application, additional claims up to a maximum of five may be designated for publication. (C) A dependent claim should not be selected unless the independent claim on which it depends is also printed. In the case where a multiple dependent claim is selected, the entire chain of claims for one embodiment should be listed. (D) In reissue applications, the broadest claim with changes or the broadest additional reissue claim should be selected for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed subpoints; ensure consistency between claims selected and figure selected for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record figure selected for printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners preparing a non-IFW application for issue are to record the figure selected for printing in the Official Gazette in the box labeled 'Print Fig.' on the face of the file wrapper, or if IFW application, on the Issue Classification sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily a single figure is selected. The figure should be consistent with the claim to be printed and must not be one labeled 'prior art.' If there is no figure illustrative or helpful, 'None' may be written. It is no longer necessary for drawings to be stamped approved or for the examiner to write this information by the Draftsperson’s stamp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of examiner-cited references (PTO-892 or IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: All references which have been cited by the examiner during the prosecution, including those appearing in Board decisions or listed in reissue oath, must be listed on either form PTO-892 or on an Information Disclosure Statement (PTO/SB/08, old PTO-1449) and initialed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References listed by an examiner on a PTO-892 will be indicated with an asterisk in the 'References Cited' section of the patent front page. An asterisk indicates only that the examiner listed the reference on PTO-892 and conveys no further significance. The examiner lists references relied upon in a prior art rejection or mentioned as pertinent. Do not list references previously cited by applicant on an IDS on a PTO-892; no distinction is made in printed 'References Cited' for source of references. New references cited when application is in issue should be added via PTO-892 or PTO/SB/08. All copies of references placed in the file during prosecution should be retained when forwarding to Publishing Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical support verification of references
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing an application for allowance, the technical support staff will verify that there is at least one list of references (PTO-892 or PTO/SB/08) in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technical support staff will also verify that each reference on the Information Disclosure Statement has either been initialed by the examiner or lined-through by the examiner. All lists of references are maintained in the center section of any paper file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of erroneous citations
rubrics_metrics.description: In any application otherwise ready for issue in which an erroneous citation has not been formally corrected in an official paper, the examiner is directed to correct the citation by an examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 707.05(g) for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion after interference
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action after termination of an interference, the examiner should make of record in each application all references not already of record which were pertinent to any preliminary motions and which were discussed in the decision on motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure references discussed in motions/decisions are included in the record post-interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and naming on file wrapper / Issue Classification Sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner and the assistant examiner involved in the allowance will print or stamp their names on the file wrapper in the appropriate boxes, or if IFW, type their names on the Issue Classification sheet. The assistant examiner shall place his or her initials after his or her typed, printed, or stamped name. The primary examiner will place his or her signature so that the typed/stamped/printed name can still be easily read. A line should be drawn through the 'Assistant Examiner' box to make clear the absence of a name was not an oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the names of the primary examiner and the assistant examiner appearing on the face of the application file wrapper or the Issue Classification Sheet will be listed in the printed patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to state reasons for allowance (37 CFR 1.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning. The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication; applicant may file a statement commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating reasons for allowance is not mandatory, but examiners are urged to ensure the application file contains a complete and accurate picture of the Office’s consideration. The practice formalizes existing authority and provides applicants opportunity to comment. Failure to respond to applicant comments does not create any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for a Statement of Reasons for Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where specific reasons are recorded, care must be taken to ensure statements are accurate, precise, and do not place unwarranted interpretations on the claims. Each statement should include at least (1) the major difference in the claims not found in the prior art of record, and (2) the reasons why that difference is considered to define patentability over the prior art if either is not clear in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements need not enumerate all reasons; where many reasons exist, stating major or important reasons may suffice, but couch appropriately. Avoid stock paragraphs or meaningless/uninformative statements. It is improper to use the statement to attempt to narrow a claim by providing a special definition not supported in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to add Reasons for Allowance — illustrative indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative examples when a statement should likely be added include: (A) claims allowed on the basis of one/some of a number of arguments/affidavits where a statement is necessary to identify which were persuasive (appeal brief, ordinary reply, affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 plus arguments under 102/103); (B) first action issue of a noncontinuing or continuing application where differences are not discussed elsewhere; (C) withdrawal of a rejection for reasons not suggested by applicant; (D) allowance after remand from the Board; (E) allowance coincident with citation of newly found references that are very close to the claims but claims considered patentable thereover; (F) where reasons are of record but unclear or spread throughout file history; (G) allowance based on a claim interpretation not readily apparent; (H) allowance following court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines are illustrative—not exhaustive—and intended to aid the examiner's judgment whether the record 'as a whole' makes clear the reasons for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of suitable and unsuitable statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual provides concrete examples of suitable statements (e.g., primary reason is inclusion of a specific limitation, telephonic interview agreed amendment, claims deemed nonobvious improvement, grant of effective filing date) and examples of unsuitable content (e.g., vague mechanical descriptions without explanation, 'main reasons are applicant’s remarks', blanket assertions of novelty/nonobviousness without support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include matter not relating directly to reasons for allowance. Unsuitable statements include those that are unclear, conclusory, or that attempt to create definitions or broad legal positions not supported by the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and form for attaching Statement of Reasons for Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner finds a need to place a statement in the file at time of allowance, the examiner should (a) check the appropriate box on form PTOL-37 and (b) attach a paper containing the examiner's statement of reasons for allowance. The statement should be typewritten, identify the application number, be clearly labeled 'Statement of Reasons for Allowance,' and specify that comments may be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 13.03 may be used; the statement should preferably be submitted with the issue fee to avoid processing delays. A similar form paragraph 13.03.01 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter prior to allowance in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant comments on examiner's Statement of Reasons for Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s statement is the personal opinion of the examiner as to why the claims are allowable and should not create an estoppel; only applicant's statements create estoppel. Applicant may comment and set forth position if disagreeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should preferably be submitted no later than payment of the issue fee and should be labeled 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Allowance.' Such comments will be entered in the application file by the Office of Publication. The application file generally will not be returned to the examiner after entry of such comments; absence of examiner response does not indicate agreement. Examiner may review and comment but has no obligation to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowance — timing and fees (37 CFR 1.311)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on examination, it appears applicant is entitled to a patent, a Notice of Allowance will be sent specifying the issue fee which must be paid within three months from date of mailing of the notice to avoid abandonment. The three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice may also include the publication fee for applications subject to publication; issue fee and publication fee must both be paid within three months. Authorization to charge an applicant's deposit account may be filed only after mailing of the Notice of Allowance; submission of an incorrect issue fee or a completed transmittal form after mailing operates as a request to charge the deposit account. The Notice of Allowance mailing date is recorded on the paper or image file wrapper table of contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL-85 Notice of Allowance form and patent term extension/adjustment statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTOL-85 Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due form has been revised to include publication fee information and patent term extension or adjustment amounts; the form is three pages with the PTOL-85B to be returned with payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are three versions of page three depending on filing date: (A) filed before June 8, 1995 — no term adjustment applies, (B) filed on/after June 8, 1995 and before May 29, 2000 — may be eligible for patent term extension per 35 U.S.C. 154(b), (C) filed on/after May 29, 2000 — may be eligible for patent term adjustment per 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.702-1.705. Applicants are reminded to transmit an extra copy of PTOL-85B when paying by deposit account authorization. See USPTO website for information about eighteen-month publication, publication fees, and patent term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments received after allowance / Issue Notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed under 37 CFR 1.312, see MPEP § 714.15 to § 714.16(e); if the amendment contains claims copied from a patent, see MPEP § 2307.03. Any paper filed after receiving the Issue Notification should include the indicated patent number, unless the application has been withdrawn from issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to an Issue Batch Number is no longer necessary because the Office no longer stores and tracks applications according to issue batches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undelivered Notice of Allowance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Notice of Allowance is returned and a new notice is sent, the date of sending the notice must be changed in the file to agree with the remailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is an IFW application, retain the original document, a copy of the returned document with any markings, and the remailed document in the application so the file history is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowance not withheld due to inventor death (unless executor intervenes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Allowance will not be withheld due to death of the inventor if the executor or administrator has not intervened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 409.01(f) for related practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy Order applications and jurisdiction after D-10 Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy Order applications are not sent to issue even when claims have been allowed; instead of mailing a Notice of Allowance, a D-10 Notice is sent. If the Secrecy Order is withdrawn after the D-10 notice is mailed, treat the application as ordinary and in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction of the application remains with the primary examiner until the Notice of Allowance is mailed. The examiner may make examiner’s amendments correcting obvious errors and may admit 37 CFR 1.312 amendments confined to matters of form or cancellation of claims; the examiner’s action on other 1.312 amendments consists of a recommendation to the Director. To regain jurisdiction the examiner must write a letter to the Director requesting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on USPTO action after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the patent has been granted, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office can take no action concerning it, except as provided in 35 U.S.C. 135; 35 U.S.C. 251–256; 35 U.S.C. 302–307; and 35 U.S.C. 311–316.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the statutory post-grant processes available; routine Office corrections are limited after grant.
